Sept 1, 2026

Given a set of variables, create batch assignments that are as orthogonal as possible by minimizing the canonical correlation between batch and study design

```{r min.cca}
# https://chatgpt.com/c/6a96ba1d-bed4-83ea-9010-2b0ba644a9cd
minimize_category_cca <- function(
  Z, K,
  sizes = NULL,
  objective = c("largest", "sum_squared"),
  n_starts = 20,
  max_iter = 100,
  seed = NULL
) {
  objective <- match.arg(objective)

  Z <- as.matrix(Z)
  Z <- scale(Z)
  Z <- Z[, apply(Z, 2, sd) > 1e-10, drop = FALSE]
  Z <- Z[,colSums(apply(Z, 2, is.na))==0, drop=FALSE]

  n <- nrow(Z)

  if (is.null(sizes)) {
    sizes <- rep(n %/% K, K)
    sizes[seq_len(n %% K)] <- sizes[seq_len(n %% K)] + 1L
  }

  stopifnot(length(sizes) == K, sum(sizes) == n)

  if (!is.null(seed))
    set.seed(seed)

  qz <- qr(Z)
  rank_z <- qz$rank
  Qz <- qr.Q(qz)[, seq_len(rank_z), drop = FALSE]

  cca_objective <- function(group) {
    # K-1 full-rank category contrasts
    X <- model.matrix(~ factor(group))[, -1, drop = FALSE]
    X <- scale(X, center = TRUE, scale = FALSE)

    # Orthonormal bases avoid explicit covariance inverses
    qx <- qr(X)

    rank_x <- qx$rank

    if (rank_x == 0L || rank_z == 0L)
      return(0)

    Qx <- qr.Q(qx)[, seq_len(rank_x), drop = FALSE]

    rho <- svd(crossprod(Qx, Qz), nu = 0, nv = 0)$d
    rho <- pmin(rho, 1)

    if (objective == "largest")
      max(rho)
    else
      mean(rho^2)
  }

  best_group <- NULL
  best_value <- Inf

  for (start in seq_len(n_starts)) {
    group <- sample(rep(seq_len(K), sizes))
    value <- cca_objective(group)

    for (iter in seq_len(max_iter)) {
      improved <- FALSE
      order_i <- sample.int(n)

      for (i in order_i) {
        candidates <- sample(which(group != group[i]))

        for (j in candidates) {
          proposal <- group
          proposal[c(i, j)] <- proposal[c(j, i)]

          proposal_value <- cca_objective(proposal)

          if (proposal_value < value - 1e-10) {
            group <- proposal
            value <- proposal_value
            improved <- TRUE
            break
          }
        }

        if (improved)
          break
      }

      if (!improved)
        break
    }

    if (value < best_value) {
      best_value <- value
      best_group <- group
    }
  }

  list(
    category = best_group,
    objective = best_value,
    category_sizes = tabulate(best_group, nbins = K),
    criterion = objective
  )
}
```

```{r analysis}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)

# read data
df = read_xlsx("~/Downloads/study_design.xlsx") %>%
  mutate(ID = as.character(ID))

# study design
form = ~ Diagnosis + region #+ ID
# form = ~ 0 + ID + region + Age + Sex + PMI + Group
# form = ~ 0 + ID 
Z = model.matrix(form, df)

# create batch assignments
# use K = 8 batches
fit <- minimize_category_cca(
  Z,
  K = 8,
  objective = "sum_squared",
  n_starts = 100,
  seed = 1
)

table(LETTERS[fit$category])
fit$objective

# fit$category = rep(1:6, 4)

# create design matrix
data = LETTERS[fit$category] %>%
  data.frame(Cat=., row.names=df$sID) %>%
  cbind(df)

X = model.matrix(~0+Cat, data)

# confirm with CCA
it = cancor(X, Z)
mean(it$cor^2)

# Batch assignments created here
data %>%
  select(Cat)

# counts of Diagnosis within each Cat
with(data, table(Cat, Diagnosis))

# counts of region within each Cat
with(data, table(Cat, region))

# counts of ID within each Cat
with(data, table(Cat, ID))
```
